visionMissionContent.title: Vision & Mission
visionMissionContent.intro: The Department of Nutrition and Food Science at KNUST prepares graduates who advance food systems, public health, and innovation across Ghana and beyond.
visionMissionContent.vision: To be Africa's leading hub for nutrition science, food innovation, and community-centred health education—producing graduates who transform food systems and improve lives.
visionMissionContent.mission: We deliver rigorous academic programmes, hands-on research, and industry partnerships that equip students and faculty to solve real-world challenges in nutrition, food safety, and sustainable food production.

values.title: Excellence
values.description: Evidence-based teaching, research integrity, and continuous improvement in all programmes.

values.title: Community
values.description: Outreach, alumni engagement, and partnerships that connect campus learning to public impact.

values.title: Innovation
values.description: Entrepreneurship, product development, and technology applied to food and nutrition challenges.

values.title: Inclusion
values.description: Accessible pathways for diverse learners—from undergraduate study through doctoral research.

hodWelcome.name: Prof. Angela Parry-Hanson Kunadu
hodWelcome.message: Welcome to the Department of Nutrition and Food Science. We are committed to training ethical leaders, advancing food and nutrition research, and partnering with communities and industry to improve health outcomes across Ghana and beyond. eventPreview.title: Food Fraud and Traceability: Site Visit
eventPreview.description: Tour a large-scale facility's quality control lab and attend a briefing on how they use technology to combat food

sections.heading: Event Overview
sections.body: This immersive site visit gives food science and nutrition students direct exposure to the quality-control systems that protect consumers and preserve trust across the supply chain.

sections.heading: What You Will Learn
sections.body: Participants will see traceability workflows, fraud detection tools, quality assurance checkpoints, and documentation practices used by leading food businesses.

sections.heading: Who Should Attend
sections.body: This event is ideal for students, recent graduates, alumni, entrepreneurs, lecturers, and industry partners interested in food technology, quality assurance, and responsible innovation.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: Food fraud threatens public health and weakens consumer confidence. The visit connects classroom theory to practical controls that improve safety, transparency, and accountability.

sections.heading: Registration Details
sections.body: Spaces are limited. Register early, arrive on time, and bring a valid student or professional ID for verification at the venue.

sections.heading: About Scholarship
sections.body: The NFS Leadership Scholarship is more than just a financial award; it is an investment in the next generation of innovators and community architects. Sponsored by Nonprofit Financial Services, this scholarship recognizes students who don't just see the world as it is, but as it could be. We look for Difference Makers, young leaders who demonstrate a unique blend of academic excellence and an entrepreneurial drive to solve local challenges. By removing financial barriers, the NFS Achieve program empowers students to take their vision to the next level, fostering a legacy of leadership that strengthens our economy and our communities.

sections.heading: Key Values to Highlight:
body: Entrepreneurship: A focus on business-minded problem-solving.
Resilience: Overcoming obstacles to achieve educational goals.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
body: Open to female students currently enrolled or planning to enroll in an accredited undergraduate or graduate program in technology or engineering.
Must demonstrate academic excellence, with a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Commitment to advancing technology solutions for sustainable development.
A letter of recommendation from a professor, mentor, or supervisor.

sections.heading: Application Requirements:
body: Resume/CV highlighting academic and professional achievements
500-word personal statement on your vision for sustainable technology and how this scholarship will help achieve it

sections.heading: Benefits of the Scholarship:
body: Financial assistance to support tuition, books, or educational supplies
Mentorship opportunities with industry leaders in tech
Invitation to attend exclusive webinars and workshops on renewable tech and business innovation
Access to a network of like-minded female tech leaders and influencers

sections.heading: Selection Process:
sections.body: Applications are evaluated based on academic excellence, personal statement, and commitment to sustainable technology. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a brief interview with the scholarship committee.

sections.heading: Award Announcement:
sections.body: Recipients will be notified by January 10, 2025, and will receive a certificate of achievement along with the $15,000 award.

This initiative is led by the Department of Nutrition & Food Science, University of Ghana and aligns with our mission to train future nutritionists, dietitians, and food scientists while serving Ghanaian communities through outreach, research, and student experiential learning.
campaign.department: Department of Nutrition & Food Science, University of Ghana
campaign.coordinator: Dr. Ama Mensah, PhD — Food Science
objectives: Procure and maintain lab instruments aligned with current food science curricula.
Advance practical learning for NFS undergraduate and postgraduate students.
Strengthen community nutrition outcomes through evidence-based interventions.
